testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Air brakes need ____ to work.
questions.explanation: Air brakes use compressed air to work.

questions.question: A front brake limiting valve usually has two markings. They read:
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles with air brakes made before 1975 have a front brake limiting valve with two settings: "normal" and "slippery."

questions.question: A slack adjuster should move no more than ____ from the push rod.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, pull each slack adjuster to check it. It should not move more than one inch. If it moves more than one inch, it needs to be fixed.

questions.question: In cold weather, check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator:
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator stops ice from building up in air brake systems. Check and refill it every day in cold weather.

questions.question: You should not use the parking brake if:

options.text: There is snow on the ground.

questions.explanation: After coming down a steep grade, do not use the parking brake if your brakes are hot. Let them cool first or you may damage them.

questions.question: For a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, leakage during a test should be no more than ____ in one minute.
questions.explanation: In a static leakage test on a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate must not exceed 5 psi in one minute. If it leaks faster, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: Air tank drains should:

options.text: Only be used when it is wet outside.
Be used to drain the tanks completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used to drain the tanks completely.
questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and compressor oil from the tanks. Always drain the tank completely.

questions.question: Why should you drain the air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
To allow for a change in pressure

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains moisture and compressor oil. These build up in the tanks and can damage the brake system. Drain the tanks at the end of each day to clean them out.

questions.question: Having ABS on only one axle:

options.text: Still gives you more control when braking.
Slows the vehicle, but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Still gives you more control when braking.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle has ABS on only one axle, you will have more control when braking than without ABS. Brake normally.

questions.question: A ____ lets a driver apply spring brakes slowly.
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver apply spring brakes gradually. It is controlled by a lever on the dashboard.

questions.question: What do the two systems of a dual air brake system share?
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system share one air compressor. If the air compressor breaks, neither system will work.

questions.question: Do not drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check brake drums during your walk-around inspection before driving. It is unsafe to drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half of the friction area width.

questions.question: What kind of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: the service brake, the parking brake, and the emergency brake. Emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: Brake linings should be:
questions.explanation: Brake linings should not be loose or wet with oil or grease. They should not be too thin.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997, and other vehicles with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1998, must have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in an air brake system is releasing air:

options.text: You should not be concerned as this is a normal process.
There is something wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is something wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air if pressure gets too high. If the valve is releasing air, something is wrong. Have a mechanic repair it.

questions.question: If air pressure drops to ____, a visual low pressure warning signal should have already turned on.
questions.explanation: A visual low pressure warning signal should turn on before air pressure drops to between 55 and 75 psi. This signal can be a light, a buzzer, or a wig wag.

questions.question: To get normal stopping power, drivers with a front brake limiting valve should:

options.text: Set the control to the off position.
Set the control to the neutral position.

questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have front brake limiting valves with "normal" and "slippery" settings. Set the valve to "normal" to get full stopping power. The "slippery" setting reduces stopping power. Front wheel braking works well in all driving conditions.

questions.question: During an inspection, slack adjusters on S-cam brakes should not move more than:
questions.explanation: Check each slack adjuster after parking on level ground and setting wheel chocks. Pull the slack adjusters to make sure they do not move more than about one inch. If they move more than one inch, they need adjustment.

questions.question: The air compressor is connected to the:
questions.explanation: The air compressor is connected to the engine through gears or a v-belt. It may be cooled by air or by the engine cooling system.

questions.question: What does an application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
How much air pressure is available.
How much air pressure is needed to stop the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: An application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. It helps drivers know if their brakes are starting to fade.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Gives the driver more control when braking hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives the driver more control when braking hard.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) gives drivers better control during hard braking. However, it does not make the vehicle stop in a shorter distance.

questions.question: Is a low air pressure warning signal needed on vehicles with air brakes?
questions.explanation: Any vehicle with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal.

questions.question: What can happen if you don't drain air tanks?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause the brakes to fail.
The brakes become soft and squishy.
Too much air collects in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause the brakes to fail.
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and compressor oil. If water is not removed, it can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure.

questions.question: If spring brakes engage while carrying a heavy load, how long will it take to stop?
questions.explanation: Spring brakes do not work on all axles. If they engage due to low air pressure, your vehicle will need more distance to stop, especially with a heavy load.
